discovered_by: Claude, 2026-09-26, while preparing the fresh 2v2 pole certification: pole_B_genome(4) resolves to plain OP7 while every frozen 4v4 suite record names B3-3. Scope established by SUITE_4V4_POLE_B_IDENTITY_AUDIT.json (experiments/audit_4v4_pole_b_identity.py). Invalidation authorized by PI the same day.

THE_DEFECT.summary: The 4v4 suite distillation dataset was collected, and all four distilled students were evaluated, against plain OP7 (SDS_PARENT_OP7, overlay {min_alive_for_defender: 4}) -- the Pole B that FAILED 4v4 certification. The frozen protocol specifies the certified B3-3 Pole B (SDS2_B3_LOCKDEF10_2V1, overlay {lock_defender: 10, enable_2v1: true, min_alive_for_defender: 4}).
THE_DEFECT.what_was_actually_installed: opponent_spec.pole_B_genome(4), pole_config_hash 60324f4af93a..., vs certified B3-3 pole_config_hash ee1cab774896...
THE_DEFECT.mechanism: pole_attestation.resolve_pole_genome fell back silently to pole_B_genome(n) whenever --pole-b-genome-json was not passed. The suite collector and the suite sharing evaluator never passed it -- they did not even accept that argument -- and called pole_B_genome() directly. The specialist trainer and the Separated evaluator did pass it and also attested the live pole against the certification, which is why the teacher and Separated runs were correct.
why_no_check_caught_it: run_state.seal's audit verifies rows, seed blocks, checkpoint pins and statistics; by its own statement it does not certify the experimental design, and pole identity is not among its checks
the Layer-2 cross-scale attestation checks that each stage is one module across scales; both pole paths ran through the same modules
the suite dataset manifest and the suite crossover records carried no pole identity at all, so nothing downstream could compare
THE_DEFECT.same_class_as: PI_B3_TRAIN_EVAL_POLE_MISMATCH_INVALIDATION.json -- the same silent fallback, one stage further downstream

on_plain_OP7.SUITE_DISTILLATION_4V4 dataset collectio: CODE_PATH_NO_OVERRIDE: collect_suite_distillation_states_4v4.py @ ae89f636 (first commit; the file was untracked when it ran on 2026-09-24) installs pole_B_genome(N_AGENTS) and accepted only --device, --smoke, --n-per-pole. The manifest records no pole.
on_plain_OP7.four student crossovers: CODE_PATH_NO_OVERRIDE: eval_suite_sharing_crossover_4v4.py @ ae89f636 line 114 installs pole_B_genome(N_AGENTS) and accepted no Pole-B argument. opponent_spec.py unchanged since 81d0d6fe (2026-09-05), so pole_B_genome(4) returned plain OP7 throughout.

EVIDENCE.evidence_class_caveat: CODE_PATH_NO_OVERRIDE is the weakest evidence class: no run-time record of the instantiated pole exists for these stages. It is decisive here because the producing code had no mechanism by which any other pole could have been installed.
EVIDENCE.behavioural_consistency: Student z0@PoleB win rates were 0.94-0.97 in all four arms, versus pi_A3's 0.74 on certified B3-3 -- consistent with an easier, non-demanding Pole B. Corroborating only; not used as evidence of the pole.

for_the_intended_4v4_suite_comparison: the four distilled student checkpoints as suite arms (they were trained on the wrong Pole-B state distribution)
WHAT_THIS_INVALIDATES.why_re_evaluation_alone_would_not_repair: The dataset itself was collected on plain OP7, so the students were TRAINED on the wrong Pole-B states, not merely scored on them. Re-running their crossover on B3-3 would evaluate students distilled from the wrong distribution. The dataset must be recollected and the students redistilled.
WHAT_THIS_INVALIDATES.retracted_reading: 'The distilled students reproduce the teacher pair's 4v4 Pole-B asymmetry; these reversals are not by themselves evidence that sharing destroyed specialization.' This compared a teacher Delta_B measured on B3-3 (-0.156, live-attested) with student Delta_B measured on plain OP7. It is withdrawn. The student Delta_B reversal may be an artifact of the uncertified pole.

WHAT_STAYS_VALID.the_sealed_records_themselves: The four sealed RESULT/AUDIT records are NOT edited or deleted. They remain valid, integrity-verified provenance of exactly what they measure: 'this checkpoint, evaluated on plain OP7 with these seeds, produced these numbers.' They are excluded from paper claims about the 4v4 suite.
WHAT_STAYS_VALID.pole_A_half: The dataset's Pole-A states and the students' Pole-A cells used pole_A_genome(4), which equals the certified Pole A (hash 4194fe47...). Pole A was never wrong. This does not rescue the students, which were trained on both halves.

REPAIR_PLAN.status: code repaired 2026-09-26; data repair not yet run
code: pole_attestation.certified_pole_genome: the single source of a pole -- the governing certification, rebuilding a candidate pole from its candidate_source file (the bytes training loaded) and failing closed on any overlay mismatch or missing certification
resolve_pole_genome no longer falls back silently: with no candidate it returns the certified pole

collector, sharing evaluator, Separated evaluator and specialist trainer all resolve both poles through it; the collector and sharing evaluator refuse to start if their frozen spec's POLES block disagrees with the certified pole, and every artifact now records the resolved pole identity

Layer 3 of the cross-scale identity attestation (resolved experimental-object identity) checks both the stage code paths and each artifact's recorded pole; a negative-control test feeds plain OP7 into a stage and proves it goes red
data_if_authorized: recollect SUITE_DISTILLATION_4V4 on certified B3-3 with the repaired collector (fresh registered seed block)
redistill Fully Shared+z and Share-Encoder (and Share-Backbone / Share-Macro only if the depth extension is still wanted)
rerun each forced-z crossover on B3-3 (fresh registered seed blocks) with the repaired, sealing evaluator

WHAT_MUST_NOT_BE_CONCLUDED_FROM_THE_INVA: that sharing destroys Pole-B specialization at 4v4
that the distilled students reproduce the teacher pair's asymmetry
any comparison of these four arms against the Separated arm, which was evaluated on a different Pole B
anything about the 4v4 point on the cross-scale sharing figure
